findings.reasoning: search_users interpolates the caller-supplied `name` directly into the SQL string via an f-string, unlike get_user in the same file which uses a `?` placeholder. Any quote in `name` terminates the literal and lets the caller inject SQL. For example, name="' OR '1'='1" makes the query return every user; a UNION SELECT can read other tables. Inputs with an apostrophe (e.g. O'Brien) also raise sqlite3.OperationalError, so it is a correctness bug too. Also, LIKE wildcards % and _ in input are not escaped.
findings.title: SQL injection in search_users via f-string interpolation of `name`
findings.body: Use a parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE name LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\'", (f"%{escaped}%",)) where escaped has \\, % and _ backslash-escaped.

failure_scenario.expected: No users (or only users whose name literally contains that text)
failure_scenario.actual: Query becomes ... LIKE '%' OR '1'='1%' and returns all users' ids, names and emails; a UNION payload can exfiltrate other tables, and name="O'Brien" raises OperationalError
